newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE -Floor seen at $245/T for US arb export.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE -Floor seen at $245/T for US arb export.

text.p: Asian MTBE prices remain sluggish in the absence of any fresh large regional demand but it is not expected to collapse as traders eye arbitrage opportunities to the US, industry sources said on Wednesday.
"The market is not expected to take a big fall. At around $250/T traders will try to move cargoes to the US. The market is floored at $245/T, one trader said.
Free-on-board (fob) Singapore MTBE lifting for second half May was assessed at between $250 and $260 per tonne, down from $255-$260 last week.
"I think there are sellers who are willing to conclude deals at around $255/T," the trader said.

Fundamentally, traders said the market will be awashed with supplies in June as the new 50,000 tonne per year Singapore plant would be operating at full capacity with giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) looking to raise its stocks in Singapore in preparation for the start up of a new plant in Saudi Arabia.
The Singapore plant is expected to begin commercial operations in the second half of May after facing start up problems in late April leading to a shutdown of the plant last week.
The Saudi plant or the 700,000 tonne per year Sadaf plant in Al Jubail, is targetted to start up on May 15, traders said.
Traders said there were suggestions earlier that the plant, a joint-venture between SABIC and Royal Dutch Shell, might start up as late as July.
A third plant, the 330,000 tonne per year Malaysian plant, currently maximising propylene output over MTBE is expected to resume normal production in July, traders said.
The plant is configured to produce 70 percent of MTBE and 30 percent of propylene but has the flexibilty to raise propylene output to 50 percent, they said.
Regional demand remains weak despite news of Indonesia's effort to promote the use to lower lead and unleaded gasoline.
"The consumption of gasoline that uses MTBE in Indonesia is very small. Most cars there still don't have a catalytic converter even the new Timur car," said a trader.
Firmer gasoline prices in Singapore have not helped either as it is still not economical for blenders to use MTBE to upgrade octane values.
On the tenders, Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) issued a six-month term tender to buy three to five cargoes of 3,500 tonnes of MTBE for delivery between July to December 1997.
The tender closes on May 7 and offers are valid for two days.
